name: Next.js image RCE
tile_line: Only with sharp below 0.35.5 on glibc Linux.
tldr: A memory bug in the SVG library inside sharp may let an attacker with no login run code through Next.js image optimization. No attacks reported. On glibc Linux, make sure sharp is 0.35.5 or later; a Next.js upgrade may not pull it in.
summary: The bug is in librsvg, the SVG library bundled inside `sharp`, and almost every Next.js version is affected. A separate bug fixed on 3 Nov let self-hosted sites parse an attacker's SVG even with SVG support off (the default). CISA's entry on the CVE record marks a proof of concept: the public librsvg report includes a file that triggers the bug, but no code-execution exploit is published.

affected.label: sharp older than 0.35.5
affected.text: Next.js 10.0.0 to 15.5.27 or 16.0.0 to 16.4.0 with `sharp` below 0.35.5, which bundles the unfixed librsvg. Next.js 15.5.28 and 15.5.29 still accept `sharp` 0.34.x, so an old lockfile can keep the bug after upgrading Next.js; 16.4.1 and later require 0.35.5.

affected.label: Running on glibc-based Linux
affected.text: Vercel says the code execution risk is when Next.js runs on glibc-based Linux. Alpine and other musl-based images aren't named as affected.

affected.label: The image optimizer takes an attacker's SVG
affected.text: With `dangerouslyAllowSVG: true` it does by design. With the default `false`, self-hosted sites on 15.0.0 to 15.5.28 or 16.0.0 to 16.4.4 can still be made to parse an attacker-supplied SVG at `/_next/image` (CVE-2026-119347); its advisory doesn't cover versions before 15. The advisories don't say whether Vercel-hosted sites or apps with tight image source rules are exposed.

do.label: Upgrade Next.js and check sharp
do.text: Go to 16.4.5 or 15.5.29, which fix this and the SVG bypass, then check that `npm ls sharp` shows 0.35.5 or later. Vercel says upgrading Next.js makes package managers provide a fixed `sharp`, but 15.5.28 and 15.5.29 still accept 0.34.x, so on 15.x update `sharp` yourself if it doesn't. Rebuild and redeploy.

do.label: Can't upgrade Next.js? Upgrade sharp
do.text: Vercel's workaround: make sure the `sharp` Next.js uses is 0.35.5 or later. Fresh installs get it automatically.

sources.title: Next.js GHSA-2464: image optimization RCE, versions, sharp 0.35.5 workaround
Next.js GHSA-7qx7: SVG reaches the parser even with dangerouslyAllowSVG off
CVE record: CVE-2026-96889, librsvg use-after-free (Red Hat); CISA marks "poc"
sharp v0.35.5 release (bundles the fixed librsvg)
npm registry: next 15.5.29 still accepts sharp 0.34.x
GNOME librsvg issue 1241: report and crash reproducer
Cloud Security Alliance: no exploitation reported as of 15 Oct

changes.text: Corrected the SVG bypass range (15.0.0 onwards). Vercel's claim that upgrading Next.js pulls in a fixed sharp conflicts with 15.x's dependency range. Explained why CISA's "poc" doesn't make the exploit public.
